text:
Alex: Heads up — noticed a handful of orgs reporting duplicate charge events when clients retry requests without an idempotency key. Saw this in billing stream today, ~20 events in 10m window.
Maria: ugh, ok. Are these definitely from retries or could be separate requests?
Alex: Root cause looks like retries + race across frontends. Example request missing header: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
# no Idempotency-Key header
{...} 
```
Ken: If there's no idempotency key we currently do per-key dedupe only in the request handler. Metering increments happen after routing and can race.
Grace: That matches. Our burst path uses per-connection counters with eventual flush; multiple workers each increment meter before the idempotency check completes.
Maria: Two immediate questions: 1) Short-term mitigation to stop double-charging customers; 2) Longer-term design for metering order and idempotency guarantees.
Alex: Short-term fix: detect duplicate charge patterns in billing pipeline and auto-refund when identical payload+org+timestamp within a small window. But that'll be messy for audit.
Ken: We can also change enforcement: check/record idempotency key (or compute payload fingerprint) in a fast central cache before incrementing quota. Redis with a TTL and atomic set-if-not-exists should work. Pseudocode: 
```
if redis.setnx("idem:{org}:{key}", request_id):
  redis.expire(...)
  increment_meter(...)
else:
  noop (treat as retry)
```
Grace: Need to handle missing keys though. For clients without Idempotency-Key we could compute a stable fingerprint: `sha256(org + path + body + user-agent)` but collisions and legitimate duplicate requests (different intents) are a risk.
Maria: Also think about per-key vs per-org quotas: if a single key is reused by many clients, we shouldn't let it bypass per-key throttles. We need both layers.
Alex: Telemetry: add a metric `billing.duplicate_detected` with tags {org, route, dedupe_strategy}. We need dashboard and alert when duplicates exceed baseline 0.1% of charges.
Ken: For rollout: implement redis-based dedupe in a canary deployed behind a feature flag. Start at 5% of traffic (low-risk orgs), monitor `billing.duplicate_detected` and `latency.p99`.
Grace: Implementation detail: use a Lua script to ensure check-and-increment is atomic across shards to avoid split-brain. Also add a short queue for metering to serialize increments per-org if needed.
Maria: UX: Console should surface suspected duplicate charges and let customer request manual review/refund. Add an admin action to mark idempotency-key as processed to avoid re-apply.
Alex: Also propose we add an optional response header to callers: `X-Redwood-Charged: true|retry-suppressed|no-idempotency` so customers can detect if they were billed.
Ken: Edge case: clients doing exponential backoff with jitter might still cause multiple concurrent in-flight without idempotency. Recommend we document best practice: always send `Idempotency-Key`. Add server-side 429 with `Retry-After` if dedupe cache is saturated.
Grace: For auditing, log every metering event with `idempotency_key || fingerprint`, trace_id, and `billing_event_id`. Include these in console drilldowns.
Maria: Tests: unit tests for Lua atomics, chaos tests with concurrent retry storms, e2e on canary orgs, and billing integration dry-run mode (no external charge) for first week.
ops-bot: deploy queued: rolling deploy to canary group started (build #5284). :rocket:
Alex: Timeline: PRs this week, canary next Mon, gradual ramp over 2 weeks if no regressions. I'll own rollout + dashboard panels.
Ken: I'll prototype the Lua script and dry-run collector.
Grace: I'll add console UI mocks for duplicate charge audit and the header change to SDK docs.
Maria: Thanks — please ping if you need product sign-off for refund policy copy.
Alex: Thanks team. If we see any spike outside canary we rollback immediately.
